Chapter 6: Advanced Practices — The Art of Segment Intending.
Now that you've got the basics of focus, emotion, and belief down, let’s talk about how you can bring conscious intention into the natural flow of your everyday life. This is where segment intending really shines—a simple but powerful way to gently guide your attention and energy as you move from one part of your day to the next.
So, what exactly is a “segment?” Well, think of it as any distinct part of your day. It could be waking up in the morning, heading out for your daily commute, starting a meeting at work, making dinner, or even just catching up with a friend. Each of these moments is a segment—a natural shift in your day.
Before you step into a new segment, try pausing for a moment. Ask yourself, “How do I want to feel right now? What would I love to experience in this next part of my day?” It’s not about trying to control every outcome—far from it. Instead, you’re tuning your inner state to line up with what you really want.
For example, maybe you’ve got a work call coming up. You might set the intention to feel calm and collaborative. Or, before sitting down to dinner with your family, you might decide you want to be present and truly appreciate the moment. These tiny pauses are like setting your compass before starting a journey. Sure, you can’t control every detail along the way, but you’ll definitely navigate with a lot more clarity and ease.
Here’s how you can make segment intending a natural part of your day:
First, notice when you’re about to move into something new—a different activity, a new environment, or even just a shift in your mindset.
Second, pause. Give yourself a breath and ask, “How do I want to feel in this next segment?”
And last, set a gentle intention. It could be clarity, ease, enjoyment—whatever feels right in that moment. Then just carry that intention forward as you go.
Over time, these small moments of awareness start to weave conscious creation into the fabric of your daily life. They help you stay out of old habits of worry or reactivity and build a real sense of agency and flow. Even if life gets unpredictable, segment intending lets you stay connected to your own inner guidance.
So, the next time you notice yourself stepping into something new, pause and set an intention. You’ll be amazed at how much more smoothly things unfold.
